newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BATISTUTA THE BYSTANDER FOR RONALDO SHOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BATISTUTA THE BYSTANDER FOR RONALDO SHOW.

text.p: Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta will be just another bystander at the Ronaldo show on Thursday when Fiorentina bid to beat Barcelona and their Brazilian to reach the European Cup Winners' Cup final.

The undisputed star of Florence, Batistuta is suspended for a booking during the 1-1 semifinal first leg draw in Spain in which he scored the Italian club's crucial goal and completely overshadowed Ronaldo.

"Batigol" now faces an agonising evening watching what should be a gripping match at the Stadio Artemio Franchi, with Barcelona determined to redeem an unimpressive season by throwing everything they can at the Italians.
"It's the first time I've watched such an important match from the stands and I feel the tension far more than if I were to be playing," the Argentine confided.
"It kills me not to be playing. Its one of those matches you long to play, and for a Fiorentina player its not as if you get such important chances every day."
Fiorentina won the very first Cup Winners' Cup in 1960-61 but have never won any other continental trophy.
It will be hard for them to cover the huge gap left by their Argentine captain, who hands over his armband to Portugal's Manuel Rui Costa for the evening.

In Batistuta's absence, all eyes are on the 20-year-old Ronaldo who was cheered by hundereds of fans at Pisa airport and given a special police escort of his own to the waiting team bus when Barcelona arrived on Tuesday.
Pisa and nearby Florence have a deep city rivalry going back to the Middle Ages and it was quite clear who commanded the loyalties of the fans at the airport.

In truth, the striker has already been the talk of Italy for months with newspapers providing daily updates on the latest developments in his tortured contract negotiations with Barcelona and the possibilities of a move to Rome.
Lazio have become obsessed with signing the Brazilian youngster but Ronaldo has nonetheless given every indication he wants and intends to stay in Spain.
Thursday should give Italian fans a clearer idea of his talents although it will not be Ronaldo's debut in Italy.
That happened when the country hosted the under-17 world championship in August 1991. The striker was just 14 years old and Brazil were beaten 2-1 in the quarter-finals by Ghana.
"(Barcelona) are a team ready to play away, an experienced and mature team," said English coach Bobby Robson. "We know we have to score because if we don't we will be out."
Robson can count on a virtually full-strength line-up after playing the first leg without six key players.
Former Sporting Lisbon winger Emmanuel Amunike is cup-tied but Robson can welcome back utility player Luis Enrique Martinez and overlapping defender Sergi Barjuan.
Fiorentina, for whom the cup looks the most likely way of getting back into Europe next season, get back Sweden's Stefan Schwarz, who won it with England's Arsenal in 1994.
They may be tempted to field a more defensive team but Batistuta warned coach Claudio Ranieri to stick to the team's strengths.
"Defensive play is not the way to aim at getting into the final. We must stick to our game.
"(Ronaldo) has said he wants to score a hat-trick against Fiorentina. Maybe nobody has told him that its difficult, very difficult, to score three against us," he said.
"The more he speaks, the more he fires us up."
Teams (probable):
Fiorentina - Francesco Toldo; Michele Serena, Pasquale Padalino, Lorenzo Amoruso, Vittorio Pusceddu, Sandro Cois, Stefan Schwarz, Manuel Rui Costa, Luis Oliveira, Anselmo Robbiati, Francesco Baiano.
Barcelona - to be announced.
